the performance of randomly constructed codebooks over discrete channels is asymptotically optimal, and that the birthday problem is a special case of the performance of randomly created codebooks over discrete communication channels.

the performance of random codebooks over discrete channels under a zero- error constraint is asymptotically the same as the performance of random linear codes over the binary erasure channel under a zero-error and a constant-weight constraint, that a zero-error code for a discrete channel can be obtained by a random linear code over a discrete channel with the addition of a constant-weight constraint and that the birthday problem is equivalent to the zero-error capacity of a discrete channel.

the probability of a birthday collision is the same for all uniform distributions, and that it can be approximated by the zero-error capacity of the binary symmetric channel with crossover probability equal to the probability of a collision in a uniform distribution.
